title: ui: the workbench rework
body:
**UI workbench rework: a light built-in, workspace tabs and compact rows**

The UI gets its workbench rework on top of upstream v0.19.0:

- A light workbench theme (`horizon-day`, shipped as a theme file and
  selectable from the Theme door; built-in default remains upstream dark).
- The ribbon carries a workspace tab row above the cells - one tab per
  machine mode, switching through the same undoable `LoadBuiltinMachine`
  the Machine door queued (the tabs and the stocked door were two doors
  onto one switch; the tabs stay).
- The operation page's section tabs wear purpose-drawn glyphs (six
  `sec-*` SVG masters, our own artwork), replacing stand-ins.
- The browser gets a compact chrome row (a View door, Expand all /
  Collapse all) and an ordered furniture layout.
- The viewport's floating control ribbon grows camera tools: a
  Perspective/Orthographic toggle and latched Orbit/Pan/Zoom tools.
- The built-in themes' density tokens change with the rework
  (`cell_h` 40 to 30, `cell_w` 72 to 76, `glyph_px` 24 to 16,
  `font_label` 13 to 11), kept for a tighter default; the ribbon height
  stays 66 px via the tab strip.

This issue tracks the UI workbench rework as a product-level line of
work, rated by the maintainer. The follow-up removal of the unreachable
Machine-door code path has its own issue.
